pr_comments: Marking this as a breaking change and for 4.0 since there were regression reports when we last tried to update, but thanks for starting work on this! We could be merging this once 4.0 is near. (when the test is fixed too 😬 )
Vite 4 will follow shortly after Rollup 3 is released, which is soon I think 👍
@Dunqing `main` is now targeting Vite 4. Would you be able to update this PR to address the merge conflict?

I think bumping `dotenv-expand` can be done independently without this change because we're not using the change in 9.0.0.

Also `dotenv-expand` requires `dotenv` v16. (It doesn't include peerDep though.) So I think we should upgrade it together if we are upgrading `dotenv-expand`.
https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv-expand/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#800-2022-02-03

I can make a new PR to support #10149, or do it here and close #10149, what do you think?

> I can make a new PR to support #10149, or do it here and close #10149, what do you think?

IMHO it would be better to remove bumping `dotenv-expand` from this PR and splitted into a PR that includes upgrading `dotenv`.
Would you revert the `pnpm.lock` change just in case?

Thanks for updating!

---

I just noticed that it throws an error with dotenv-expand@>=6.0.0 if a user had an env var that includes `$`.
The error is `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')` that is same with https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/6858.

With powershell, you can reproduce by running ``$env:VITE_FOO="$`f"; pnpm dev``. With bash, I guess `$VITE_FOO="\$f" pnpm dev` will do the same thing.

This is not a direct blocker of this PR, but this PR will block #10826 if merged.

Maybe we should wait for `dotenv-expand` to fix that. Or we could make a PR to `dotenv-expand` and apply that patch with `pnpm patch` for a while (It works because we are bundling `dotenv-expand`).

issue_context.title: Exposed env vars are not available
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Using an `.env` file to define environment variables, static values are passed on and available in Vue as expected. Exposing existing env vars to Vue, however, does not work and produces empty values.

I've exposed the env var using the syntax from [this comment](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/562#issuecomment-659771950).

STR:
* open reproduction
* start dev server with command `PORT=4000 npm run dev`

Expected:
`PORT` should be available from `main.js` and output `4000`.

Actual:
`PORT` is an empty string.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-bxj6nd?devtoolsheight=33&file=.env

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 11.6.1
    CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8850H CPU @ 2.60GHz
    Memory: 1.36 GB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 5.8 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 16.13.2 - ~/.nix-profile/bin/node
    npm: 8.1.2 - ~/.nix-profile/bin/npm
  Browsers:
    Brave Browser: 97.1.34.81
    Safari: 15.2
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

```shell
...
vite:config   env: {
vite:config     VITE_PORT: '',
vite:config     BASE_URL: '/',
vite:config     MODE: 'development',
vite:config     DEV: true,
vite:config     PROD: false
vite:config   },
...
```

This is about explicitly exposed env vars, not all env vars. Only if you write
```sh
VITE_PORT=$PORT
```
in a `.env` file, it should be made available in Vite.
Yes, it would be great if it did. I'm looking for a way to pass env vars into Vite, and Evan's comment from back then sounded like it should be possible.
That's what I tried, please look at the reproduction and debug output above.

I'm currently also struggling with this. I want to pass along a Docker environment variable to a `VITE_` variable so that it is available during compile time and I can access it in my JavaScript frontend and backend code, let's say a GraphQL URL for example. This is a SvelteKit app but it shouldn't make any difference.

```
VITE_GRAPHQL_URL=$GRAPHQL_URL
```

Is there any solution / workaround?

@svenjacobs The workaround that I'm currently using is to declare the env var as part of the script that I run to start vite, e. g.:
```sh
VITE_PORT=$PORT vite
```

I'm in the same situation.

Just returns an empty string.

> I'm in the same situation.
> 
> Just returns an empty string.

In my case it was an improper Docker / Docker Compose configuration. In my `Dockerfile` I had to make sure to specify the arguments which I want to pass during Docker build time as `ARG` and assign them to `ENV` variables, something like

```Dockerfile
ARG HASURA_GRAPHQL_URL
ENV VITE_HASURA_GRAPHQL_URL $HASURA_GRAPHQL_URL
```

and my `docker-compose.yml` looks like

```yaml
services:
  my-service:
    build:
      dockerfile: my-service/Dockerfile
      args:
        HASURA_GRAPHQL_URL: https://some-url
```

Maybe this helps 🤷🏼‍♂️
